comment: The cars the DBCs are built for (vehicles.py): the physical CAN buses, which bus each logical network of can_descriptor.json's messages (their bus_name) is on, the vendor DBCs every car has, and each car's inverters. Vehicle names match kmslap's drivetrain variants (python-data-analysis, kmslap/car/drivetrain.py), so a simulated car and its DBC line up by name. The default vehicle builds car.dbc, the one the firmware pins; every vehicle also builds car_<name>.dbc.

KSX.comment: can bus of KSU motorsports vehicles

cascadia_pm100.comment: Cascadia Motion PM100DX with the EMRAX 228 HV: its own DBC, as is (one per car: its IDs are fixed)

dti_hv500.comment: DTI HV500 / F-SiC (DTI's CAN map v2.5, extended IDs: packet ID << 8 | node ID; standard IDs, packet << 5 | node, would collide with the module temperatures on one bus)

amk_kw26.comment: AMK KW26-S5-FSE-4Q racing kit: Actual Values 1 / 2 and Setpoints 1, base address + node address

rwd_emrax.comment: the car as it is: EMRAX 228 HV through the chain and LSD, Cascadia PM100DX

awd_emrax_dti.comment: the EMRAX at the rear, DTI hub motors at the front

awd_emrax_amk.comment: the EMRAX at the rear, AMK hub motors at the front

4wd_dti.comment: DTI hub motors at all four wheels (no EMRAX, chain or diff)

4wd_amk.comment: AMK hub motors at all four wheels (the four-in-one KW26 box)
